en: The Scripture of the Divine Incantations of the Names of Five Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas for Removing Obstacles and Extinguishing Transgressions,
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of North India during the Northern Qi Dynasty.
At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain near the great city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus;
there were also twelve thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, headed by the bodhisattva Ajita.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying: "Maitreya!
To the east of this buddha-field, there are ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, equal in number to the atoms of hundreds of thousands of millions of worlds."

Beyond these Buddha-fields, there is a buddha-field named Liberation-Lord World (*Vimuktinātha-loka*). Within that world dwells a Buddha named Space-Virtue-Pure-Dust-Eye-Upright-Virtue-Phase-Radiance-Lotus-Vaidūrya-Light-Jewel-Body-Fragrance-Supreme-Fragrance-Offering-Complete-Manifold-Adornment-Crest-Infinite-Boundless-Sun-Moon-Radiance-Vow-Power-Adorned-Transformation-Adorned-Dharma-Realm-Born-Unobstructed-King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He currently resides wherever he pleases, traveling at will, and teaches the Dharma.

If a son or daughter of good family commits the four pārājika offenses, their transgression is grave. Even if the Jambudvīpa continent were reduced to atoms, and each atom represented one kalpa, such a person would have as many kalpas of sin as there are atoms; yet by reciting the name of this single Buddha even once and performing a single prostration, all these sins shall be utterly extinguished.
How much more so for those who, day and night, uphold, read, recite, and remember it without forgetting—the merit of such a person is inconceivable.

In that world, there is a bodhisattva named Unrivaled King of Non-obstruction (*Duranvaya-anāvaraṇa-rāja*). The Tathāgata has bestowed upon that bodhisattva the prediction that he shall attain buddhahood, with the name Śikhālakṣaṇa-candrasūryaprabha-jvālāratnapadma-dṛḍhavajrakāya-vairocanānāvaraṇanetra-paripūrṇadaśadig-raśmipramuñcana-sarvabuddhakṣetrasamantaprakāśana-lakṣaṇarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
"Furthermore, in that eastern direction, there is yet another Buddha named Sarvavyūhavimalaprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
You should also recite the name of that Buddha, honoring and respecting him:
"In the southern direction there is a Buddha named Prajñā-alaṃkāra-smaraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
One should also invoke that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, recite his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the western direction there is a Buddha named Vimalacandraprabhāsaśrīkīrti Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
You should also recite that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, invoke his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the northern direction there is a Buddha named Flower-Adorned Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
One should also invoke that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, recite his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the southeast there is a Buddha named Kārakapradīpa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
You should likewise invoke that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, recite his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the southwest there is a Buddha named Ratnottaralakṣaṇayaśas Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
One should also recite that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, and must invoke his title; one must also keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the northwest there is a Buddha named Vairocana-avalokita Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Furthermore, you should also invoke that Buddha’s name, practice respectful devotion, recite his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the northeast there is a Buddha named Abhaya-abhīru-aruṇa-roma-harṣa-nāma-saṃghoṣa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
You should also recite that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, invoke his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the direction below, there is a Buddha named Siṃhavikrāntagāmin-mūla Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
One should also recite that Buddha’s name, cultivate reverence, invoke his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind:
"In the upper direction there is a Buddha named Similar-to-the-Resplendent-King-of-Golden-Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"One should also invoke the name of that Buddha, cultivate reverence, recite his title, and keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
At that time, the Buddha told Maitreya:
"If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family with right faith who, with a sincere heart, invoke these ten..."
During the ten days following the proclamation of the names of the Buddhas, one should practice repentance for all transgressions;
one should rejoice in all the merits of all sentient beings; one should entreat all Buddhas to remain long in the world;
and one should dedicate all roots of goodness to the Dharma-realm. At that time, [the obstacles] shall be extinguished.
All transgressions shall be purified, all karmic obstructions shall be cleansed, and one shall immediately attain the full accomplishment of the adornment of all Buddha-fields;
one shall achieve the perfection of fearlessness, further attain the perfection of the marks and signs that adorn the body,
further attain the perfection of being surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas, and further attain the perfection of immeasurable dhāraṇīs.
The bhikṣuṇī further attains the fullness of immeasurable samādhis; she further attains the fullness of the adornments of buddha-fields according to her wishes;
she also attains the fullness of immeasurable spiritual friends;
and she swiftly achieves the aforementioned state of neither increase nor decrease, practicing for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi while dwelling amidst the afflictions.
One obtains the retribution of being upright and pleasing to behold, as well as an abundance of wealth and treasures;
one is always born into families of great lineage and noble clans, with a body endowed with perfect marks, and is surrounded by a retinue of harmonious and virtuous associates.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"If there be sons of good family, Or daughters of good family, etc.,
Who receive and uphold the names of these Buddhas, Throughout their successive lives, in birth after birth,"
One gains the love and respect of others, possesses great radiance and power,
becomes honored among humans in one's place of birth, and shall later attain Buddhahood.

"If there are those who personally uphold, recite, contemplate, remember, and practice these names of the infinite asaṃkhyeya Buddhas and Tathāgatas thus born, they shall have no affliction of the eyes, no affliction of the ears, nose, or tongue."

Their physical ailments shall be purified, and all obstacles shall be entirely cleansed. No one among the multitude will be able to subdue them, and they shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions shall constantly keep them in mind and always provide protection for those sentient beings.
Those Buddhas shall even manifest inconceivable skillful means and wisdom to them within their dreams, so that they may swiftly attain the gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī.
In whatever place they are born, they are never separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; they take miraculous birth within the great jewel lotuses of the Buddha’s teaching.

In every place of birth, they never abandon the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary characteristics. With the five supernormal powers and the five eyes, they teach and transform sentient beings;

they purify Buddha-fields and practice the *pāramitās* and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika-dharmas*). They do not depart from meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), the immeasurable samādhis, the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), and so forth.
He relinquishes the various powers, fearlessnesses, eloquence, and the eighteen unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma), as well as great kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity;

yet, according to the supreme calculation system of the Great Sui dynasty, which reckons immeasurable asaṃkhyeyas, he attains ten billion and ten trillion Buddha-dharmas within a single asaṃkhyeya, remaining entirely inseparable from them all.

Possessing all such merits as those of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, he in turn becomes fully endowed with such merits; he immediately attains peace and happiness, and in this way shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
If one invokes his name, one shall immediately attain inexhaustible wisdom.
If one recites his name, one shall attain the stage of non-retrogression.
If there are women who hear this Buddha’s name, this shall be their final female body, and they shall never again receive such a birth.

If one were to recite his name, even if one were to fill the world-system with sheets of gold and offer it as a gift along with the seven treasures, it would not equal even a *kalā* (one-millionth) part of the merit [derived from that recitation].”

If one invokes the name of that Buddha, the Tathāgata, immeasurable fragrances will issue from all the pores of one’s body; one shall experience the perfuming of all Buddha-fields with fragrance and further attain immeasurable and boundless merit.”

If one recites the name of that Buddha, the merit thereby obtained would not be matched even by a single *kalā* fraction of the merit gained from offering the seven treasures to fill worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, compared to merely reciting the name of that Buddha Tathāgata with one’s mouth.”
If one invokes the name of that Buddha, the Tathāgata, all the Buddha-dharmas will be completely fulfilled.

encounter the appearance of a Buddha in the world, and having seen the Tathāgata, perform immeasurable offerings and services, cultivate the holy life, and reach the further shore of all supernatural powers;
furthermore, they shall obtain a dhāraṇī named 'The Ten Transformations'."

Having seen the Tathāgata, one shall perform inconceivable offerings; one shall see Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and transcend the flow of birth and death for such *koṭi* aeons, never losing sight of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in one’s mind.

One shall obtain a body as firm and solid as Nārāyaṇa, consisting of a single bone that is difficult to bend or break; that body shall be golden in color, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.
One shall obtain the Brahma-voice, leave behind places of unrest, and attain a state of tranquility.

one ought to burn many excellent incenses.
From among those excellent incenses, many kinds emerge, foremost among them being five hundred superior varieties of aloeswood (*agaru*).
Of the superior frankincense (*guggulu*), take one and a half parts; within those one and a half parts, include *dūru* incense.
Furthermore, use three *liang* of *agaru* (aloe) incense, and the leaves of *karkarava* incense are likewise.
The finest *mushuruka* incense is added as above, along with three parts each of *tagara* and orange peel.
The proportions should be complete as follows: take one part from four parts of *kunkuma* (safflower);
ten parts of *śilā-ja* (ambergris) should be provided; two parts of *kuṅkuma* flower-fragrance;
furthermore, two parts of *agaru* (aloe) incense are required; and two parts each of *utpala* and *candana* (sandalwood) are likewise needed.
Having thus divided these into equal portions and dried them in the sun, once they are thoroughly dried, grind them into a fine powder;
then take excellent, superior honey and use it to blend with those various fragrances.
Furthermore, there are two kinds of genuine honey; separately use them to blend with that superior-grade incense.
If there is *sumana* pure oil, then use this oil to anoint both hands, and only then use the oiled hands to knead the superior incense.
Once the kneading is complete, place it in a stone vessel.
When such fragrances as these have been blended together, they are used to be burned within the Tathāgata’s stūpa.
This shall cause the Buddha’s heart to be greatly gladdened and arouse compassion for all sentient beings.
Such are the most wondrous varieties of incense, along with various sublime sounds and exquisite flowers.

yakṣas, nāgas, and kumbhāṇḍas— for their sake, he proclaimed these mantra syllables.

able to act as a guide for sentient beings, he is capable of subduing even his enemies.

Upholding the dhāraṇīs without weariness, they are likewise untiring when expounding the Dharma;

Seeing those who are worthy vessels, they are free from envy; seeing those who are fit to receive the teaching, they immediately preach for them.

or if they harbor greedy attachment to the homes of friends, or give rise to defiled craving for robes and bowls—
those such as these, bound by the fetters of desire, possess no mind of total retention or wisdom.

At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“Having heard such a name as the World-Honored One’s, If there are those with wisdom, do not be negligent.
Do not let this assembly all fail to encounter [the truth], So that they might wander through the sufferings of the evil realms.”
One should abide in the maintenance of ethical discipline and accord with patience; one should have faith in extensive learning and dwell in seclusion.
One should fulfill the most profound patience; such a person shall behold the Honored One.
Even if one has committed evil karma for hundreds of millions of eons, yet remains unaware of the retribution for that evil karma,
they shall all eventually become Buddhas, having upheld the names of these various Buddhas as described above.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, along with the assembly of bodhisattvas and great bhikṣus, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
